title: Orthogonality of a nearest-point residual
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime and let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with its extended nonarchimedean norm $|\cdot|_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $V$ be an $E$-vector space with a norm $\|\cdot\|:V\to\mathbf R_{\geq0}$ satisfying $\|av\|=|a|_E\|v\|$, $\|v+w\|\leq\max(\|v\|,\|w\|)$, and $\|v\|=0$ precisely for $v=0$. Let $n\geq0$ and suppose $b_0,\ldots,b_{n-1}\in V$ are linearly independent and satisfy the orthogonality formula
$$\left\|\sum_{i<n}a_i b_i\right\|=\max_{i<n}|a_i|_E\,\|b_i\|$$
for all $a_0,\ldots,a_{n-1}\in E$ (for $n=0$ the family is empty and both sides are $0$). Put $W=\operatorname{span}_E\{b_i:i<n\}$. Let $x\in V$ with $x\notin W$, and let $w\in W$ satisfy $\|x-w\|=\inf_{u\in W}\|x-u\|$. Then $b_n=x-w$ is nonzero and the displayed orthogonality formula holds for the enlarged family $b_0,\ldots,b_n$, that is, $\|\sum_{i\leq n}a_ib_i\|=\max_{i\leq n}|a_i|_E\|b_i\|$ for all $a_0,\ldots,a_n\in E$; in particular $b_0,\ldots,b_n$ are linearly independent and span $W+Ex$.

proof.text: Put $b=x-w$ and $d=\|b\|$. If $b=0$, then $x=w\in W$, contrary to $x\notin W$; thus $b\ne0$ and $d>0$ by definiteness. For every $z\in W$, the minimizing hypothesis gives $d\le\|x-z\|$: the infimum is at most each member of the nonempty set of distances (it contains $\|x\|$ since $0\in W$ and is bounded below by $0$).

proof.text: Fix $u\in W$ and $a\in E$. If $a=0$, then $\|u+ab\|=\|u\|=\max(\|u\|,|a|_E d)$. If $a\ne0$, put $z=w-a^{-1}u\in W$. Then $u+ab=a(x-z)$, so homogeneity and the preceding minimality inequality give $\|u+ab\|=|a|_E\|x-z\|\ge |a|_E d$. This proves that lower bound for all $a$, including $a=0$.

source.place: Agent auxiliary to paragraph (3), direct-image coefficient argument; the source paragraph does not state or prove this norm lemma. Elementary nearest-point residual calculation supplied here; external reference WANTED. Step 2.

proof.text: Write $A=\|u\|$, $B=|a|_E d$ and $R=\|u+ab\|$. The ultrametric inequality gives $R\le\max(A,B)$, while the preceding step gives $R\ge B$. If $A\le B$, these bounds force $R=B$. If $A>B$, apply the ultrametric inequality to $u=(u+ab)+(-ab)$ to get $A\le\max(R,B)$; hence $R\ge A$ and $R=A$. Here $\|-ab\|=\|ab\|=B$ follows from homogeneity and $|-1|_E=1$. Thus in both cases $\|u+ab\|=\max(\|u\|,|a|_E d)$.

proof.text: For arbitrary $a_0,\ldots,a_n$, take $u=\sum_{i<n}a_i b_i\in W$ and $a=a_n$. The assumed old orthogonality formula gives $\|u\|=\max_{i<n}|a_i|_E\|b_i\|$. Substituting this equality into the preceding two-term formula and using $b_n=b$ proves $\|\sum_{i\le n}a_i b_i\|=\max_{i\le n}|a_i|_E\|b_i\|$. For $n=0$, $u=0$ and the old maximum is $0$, so this same calculation is precisely the homogeneity identity for $a_0b$.

proof.text: If $\sum_{i\le n}a_i b_i=0$, the formula just proved implies $|a_n|_E d\le0$. Since $d>0$ and the absolute value vanishes only at $0$, $a_n=0$. The relation reduces to $\sum_{i<n}a_i b_i=0$, and the assumed independence of the old family implies $a_i=0$ for every $i<n$. This is exactly linear independence of the enlarged family, also when the old family is empty.

source.place: Agent auxiliary to paragraph (3), direct-image coefficient argument; the source paragraph does not state or prove this norm lemma. Elementary nearest-point residual calculation supplied here; external reference WANTED. Step 5.

proof.text: The span of the enlarged family is $W+Eb$. Since $b=x-w$ with $w\in W$, every $u+ab$ equals $(u-aw)+ax\in W+Ex$. Conversely $x=b+w$, so every $u+ax$ equals $(u+aw)+ab\in W+Eb$. These two inclusions give $W+Eb=W+Ex$, the asserted span.
